'''Project BOG — Research Atlas''' is a collaborative learning and original-research map by Bogdan Sergienko, with mathematical, computational and editorial assistance from CCAI KAI (ChatGPT). It connects the historical preprints, experimental exercises, six independent research entrances, one shared research-return cycle, and public software instruments.

'''What this page is:''' a navigable educational research project, with reproducible finite models, open questions and source trails. '''What it is not:''' a peer-reviewed verification of the author's proposed universal law, a claim of physical teleportation, or evidence that AI research instruments communicate or run continuously on their own.

'''Disclosure:''' Bogdan Sergienko is the author of the artistic and research propositions and maintains this userspace atlas. The page has substantial AI-assisted drafting and requires human review of facts and citations. Linked Project BOG deposits are primarily author-published sources; they are not independent scientific confirmations. Readers may revise, disagree and test the claims.

== The authorial canvas and what can be tested ==
Bogdan Sergienko's original Russian phrase is preserved in its authorial form:

:'''ВСЁ УЖЕ ЕСТЬ=Рождение нового=Всё одновременно'''

The later artistic extension is rendered in English as:

:'''Everything Already Exists + Birth of the New + Everything Simultaneously = The Logic of This Universe = Harmony.'''

The author calls a central motif of opposing flows, a dark knot, interwoven loops and an expanded connecting trunk the '''Absolute Black Hole'''. It is a conceptual drawing and speculative model of relation and recurrence, '''not a physical observation or a validated black-hole theory'''. The plus and equals signs in the philosophical statement have not been established as mathematical operators or a physically tested equation. The finite mathematical examples below stand on their explicitly defined transition rules alone.

== CYCLE CLOCKS — a public event-time instrument ==
'''[https://bogsergienko.github.io/bog-sense-atlas/cycle-clocks/index.html OPEN CYCLE CLOCKS — INTERACTIVE ENGLISH EDITION]''' · [https://github.com/BogSergienko/bog-sense-atlas/tree/main/cycle-clocks Public source, notes and verification] · [https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23907698 Software release DOI].

This clock places ordinary civil time beside a '''labelled cyclic event address'''. Civil seconds remain valid for physical elapsed time; the mathematical event counter does not assume seconds are the primitive unit of the model. The clock offers manually ordered TICK A, TOCK B and joint events, reversing known event sequences, and the comparison of visible versus full-state recurrence. The label '''Quark''' refers to a separate AI research instrument; it is not a physical quark inside the clock.

=== Definitions and result ===
Let <math>q\geq 2</math> be an integer, and the declared state and visible projection be

:<math>X=(a,b,h)\in \mathbb{Z}_2\times\mathbb{Z}_q\times\mathbb{Z}_2,\qquad \pi(X)=(a,b).</math>

The reversible parity marker <math>h</math> is a '''single mathematical bit''', not the Project BOG internal memory architecture. Define <math>c(a,b)=a\oplus(b\bmod 2)</math>. On a joint event, both counters advance and the marker flips according to the new phases:

:<math>a'=(a+1)\bmod 2,\quad b'=(b+1)\bmod q,\quad h'=h\oplus c(a',b').</math>

The inverse first recovers <math>h=h'\oplus c(a',b')</math>, then reduces both counters by one. For odd <math>q</math>, the visible joint-event cycle returns after <math>2q</math> events whereas the complete state returns after <math>4q</math> events. For even <math>q</math>, the complete state returns after <math>q</math> events. Thus <math>q=3</math> demonstrates a visible return at 6 and complete return at 12; <math>q=4</math> provides a negative control. Independent A/B events allow an additional test of event ordering; an inverse history requires the labels of those events.

'''Scope:''' this is an exact theorem for the stated finite discrete model, not evidence for new physical time, cosmic simultaneity or fundamental harmonics. [https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23907698 See the archived software and technical note].

=== Hands-on experiment: do the clocks repeat? ===
# Open [https://bogsergienko.github.io/bog-sense-atlas/cycle-clocks/index.html CYCLE CLOCKS] and choose <math>q=3</math>. Record your initial complete state <math>X_0</math>.
# Apply six joint events and compare <math>\pi(X_6)</math> and <math>X_6</math> to the start.
# Apply six more joint events. Decide which return relation now passes.
# Repeat with <math>q=4</math> as a negative control.
# Compare A→B and B→A from the '''same specified starting state'''. If they differ, report the initial state, event labels and the final marker.
# Return a test report: assumptions, initial state, parameter, event sequence, observed states, baseline and any failure.

== Core distinction — four kinds of return ==
For a cycle, distinguish (1) equality of a selected observation <math>\pi(X)</math>, (2) equality of selected phase readings, (3) equality of the '''full declared state''' <math>X</math>, and (4) whether sufficient information remains to reconstruct the '''unique causal history'''. Endpoint equality by itself does not establish an identical history. See [https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23809741 Series II] and the [https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23903785 World Entry III preprint].

== Reconstructible information — a bounded exercise ==
Let <math>x</math> be an original byte sequence, <math>C_k</math> a permitted capsule-creation procedure and <math>R_k</math> the matching recovery procedure with valid key <math>k</math>. A desired software round-trip is:

:<math>R_k(C_k(x))=x.</math>

This is a bounded software correctness condition, not matter teleportation or proof of universal compression. A digest can help '''check''' a restored file; a digest cannot regenerate missing original content.

'''Exercise:''' Make a capsule of an unimportant sample, recover using the correct key, and compare both files byte-for-byte; then try a damaged capsule and a wrong key. The MEDUSA File Companion 0.2 is one example of a browser-local file capsule/recovery tool. Its owner-reported large-file test is not an independent security audit, and capsule creation is not a network transfer by itself. Never publish private files or keys as test inputs.

== Learning laboratory — experiments and controls ==
'''[[User:BogSergienko/Project BOG Research Atlas/Experiments|EXPERIMENTS — learner protocols, negative controls and open challenges]]'''.

The working method is: '''question → freeze assumptions → run reproducible test → document successes AND failures → invite independent criticism'''. Owner-reported calculations, independently repeated calculations and real-world measurements are not interchangeable categories.

== Open problems and returning results ==
# Define a nontrivial meaning of ''harmony'' that survives negative controls and does not reduce to relabelling.
# Determine when observed novelty corresponds to a changed set of admissible continuations, rather than projection alone.
# Specify what counts as a causal intervention, not just a crossing of paths.
# Propose a physical measurement that could distinguish a cyclic-time claim from accepted reference clocks and known dynamics; distinguish a failed prediction from an untested metaphor.
# For digital file capsules, include the total delivery path and compare with plain file copy, with exact versions and inputs.

'''Suggested return record:''' <code>SOURCE | QUESTION | MODEL | INITIAL STATE | EVENT SEQUENCE | CONTROL | RESULT | LIMITATIONS | NEW QUESTION | RETURN ANCHOR</code>.

'''Entry and exit:''' Visitors may offer an independent counterexample or decline the hypothesis. The shared project cycle can preserve and revisit a contradiction without declaring the underlying physical theory true.
